messages:
irene.cs: Customer reported embedding charges that look ~2x what the dashboard shows. They sent 3 inputs in one request but invoice shows 6 embedding units. They claim dashboard shows 3 vectors (512d) but invoice billed for 6. Any quick ideas?

sam.eng: Do we have the request_id / X-Request-ID and the exact API call? Could be double-counting on our metering side for batched requests.

irene.cs: Provided the curl and request headers from the customer: ```curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \n -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-XXX' \n -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \n -d '{"model":"embed-rl-1024","inputs":["long text...","short text","another text"]}'```
Customer also included response headers: `X-Request-ID: rq_9b1f2a` and `x-metering-version: v1`.

jess-ml: Thanks — quick notes from ML infra: we've seen a bug in the old metering bridge when multi-input batches include empty-string separators or when clients send mixed object/text payloads. The bridge would expand the batch on the metering side (counts each fragment) while the serving runtime consumed the batch correctly, so dashboard (derived from runtime) shows 3 but billing (from metering events) shows 6.

jess-ml: Repro steps I ran locally: 1) send 3 inputs in one JSON array 2) inject a trailing newline in input[1] 3) metering.log shows: `metering.events: input_count=6, batch_id=b-abc123` while runtime logs show `runtime: inputs=3, embeddings_emitted=3`.

jess-ml: Sample internal log snippet: ```2026-02-28T15:12:03Z metering-service INFO event={"batch_id":"b-abc123","count":6} \n2026-02-28T15:12:03Z runtime INFO processed=3 model=embed-rl-1024 ids=[r1,r2,r3]```

billing-bot: Ticket created: CS-8792 — assigned to billing/eng-infra. Link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/CS-8792

mike-support: Two actionable items for support/customer: 1) can you ask the customer to share the X-Request-ID (we have rq_9b1f2a from them, thanks) and attach full request body including whitespace/newlines, and 2) give them a quick workaround: send inputs as separate requests or set header `X-Disable-Auto-Batch: true` until we hotfix.

irene.cs: Customer sent full body — they had a trailing "\n" inside one input and they were batching multiple short strings with an extra separator. I pushed that to the ticket.

jess-ml: Root cause summary: metering bridge was splitting on newline separators for text arrays in a legacy codepath when `inputs` included unstructured strings. This caused per-input accounting to double-count fragments. Also flagged: model aliasing caused one response to report 1536 dims for one item in one test run (mis-routed to a different embedding family) — separate bug, but not affecting charges (metering counts are independent of vector dim).

jess-ml: Fix plan: patch the bridge to canonicalize the inputs array before emitting metering events (ensure 1:1 mapping). Hotfix scheduled for next deploy (ETA ~2h). Will reconcile historical metering events for affected batches in CS-8792.

mike-support: For immediate mitigation we credited the difference for the customer's March invoice and logged the credit in CS-8792. Please confirm once hotfix is live so we can close the ticket.

irene.cs: Confirmed customer accepted the credit, happy with workaround. Thanks team! :thumbsup:

jess-ml: After hotfix deploy I'll run a sweep: query metering.events where batch_id like 'b-%' and X-Request-ID==rq_9b1f2a and generate reconciliation diff. I'll post the script here once done.

irene.cs: Please keep me updated in the ticket; closing Slack thread when hotfix done.

mike-support: Noted — closing on Slack. Follow-up in CS-8792 with credit details and postmortem. :white_check_mark:
